explanation: Wide, horizontal pupils give grazing animals a panoramic view of the ground for spotting predators, and their eyes rotate to stay level as they lower their heads to graze.

claims.text: Goats and sheep have horizontally elongated, roughly rectangular pupils.
Goats and sheep do not have vertical-slit, round or W-shaped pupils.
Horizontal pupils give grazing animals a wide view along the ground, helping them spot predators.
Goat and sheep eyes rotate to keep their pupils roughly level with the ground when the head is lowered to graze.
